R238.note: WebUtility.HtmlEncode on the tainted Message at the element-body interpolation point; RequestedAt, content type and the WriteAsync call are untouched.

R239.note:
Both query values HTML-encoded before concatenation into

body text; null query values still concatenate as empty, so legitimate output is unchanged.

R240.note: Explicit caller.Role != "admin" check before body parsing and the sink, 403 distinct from the existing 401, matching the handler's documented admin-only contract; assumes the role literal is "admin", which is stated.

R241.note: setSecure(true) on SomeCookie; the only other change is the diagnostic message text updated to 'true', which the write-up states.

R242.note: Bare-filename requirement plus realpath() separator-terminated containment closes wrapper, absolute-path and symlink escapes, but rejecting any '/' also refuses subdirectory paths like sub/report.pdf that the original served from inside reports/ - stated, but a restriction beyond the original contract.

R243.note: Named :startDate/:endDate placeholders via Sequelize replacements remove the concatenation and the values are escaped by Sequelize, closing the vector; the explanation slightly mislabels replacements as driver-side binding (that is the bind option), but the code is correct and behaviour for legitimate dates is unchanged.

R244.note: Identical markup moved into a parsed html/template with Execute writing to the ResponseWriter, giving contextual escaping of Author and Excerpt; Content-Type header and error return preserved.

R245.note: jinja2.sandbox.SandboxedEnvironment(autoescape=True) replaces the plain Environment with identical from_string/render calls, blocking the __class__/__mro__ introspection chain while preserving the 200/400 paths and the same user/campaign context; residual public-method exposure is flagged openly.

R246.note: Order() receives only a clause built from an allowlisted column map and ASC/DESC constants, never the input; empty sort remains a no-op as before, invalid sort maps to the same 500 the original produced on bad SQL, and the allowlist is what the stated contract calls for.

R247.note: lockoutOnFailure: true re-enables Identity lockout and the added IsLockedOut branch surfaces it with the standard Identity message; the lockout of an account after repeated failures is the intended fix and is stated plainly.

R248.note: field_index >= MAX_FIELDS check before the table read, returning the function's existing -1 error code; uint8_t makes a lower bound unnecessary and handle_frame already propagates the failure.
